lymph node metastasis with extracapsular extension

concepts.why: The patient presented with a left cervical lesion, and histopathology revealed a Breslow depth of 2.6 mm, 7 mitoses/mm2, and a BRAF V600E mutation, which are all characteristic of cutaneous melanoma.
The patient developed lymph node metastasis with extracapsular extension and locoregional recurrence with skin metastasis, indicating metastatic melanoma.
The patient's melanoma was found to be positive for the BRAF V600E mutation, which is a common genetic alteration in melanoma.
The patient's melanoma had a Breslow depth of 2.6 mm and 7 mitoses/mm2, which are characteristic of nodular melanoma.
The patient's melanoma had a broadened network and darkening on dermoscopy, which are characteristic of superficial spreading melanoma.
The patient's melanoma had a broadened network and darkening on dermoscopy, which are characteristic of lentigo maligna melanoma.
The patient's melanoma had a broadened network and darkening on dermoscopy, which are characteristic of acral lentiginous melanoma.
The patient's melanoma had a broadened network and darkening on dermoscopy, which are characteristic of desmoplastic melanoma.
